I'm particularly interested in AI, robotics, and software development. I have experience with Python, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and I've worked on several projects involving web development and AI-based solutions.

summary: ATHR is an interactive Mars exploration platform that brings scattered NASA data into one 3D/2D globe. Users select a point or search a place name such as Jezero and instantly see real elevation, a local slope estimate, nearby Perseverance waypoints and the rover's route. A built-in bilingual (Arabic and English) AI assistant explains the selected location using only data our backend retrieves from NASA sources. It lists its sources, reports a confidence level, and states clearly when data is missing instead of guessing or calling terrain safe. ATHR addresses the challenge by making NASA's open Mars data easy to explore, understand and question in one place. It matters because Mars data is hard for students and explorers to combine, and AI explanations of science are only trustworthy when they are traceable and honest about their limits.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

ATHR is an interactive Mars exploration platform. Users explore a 3D/2D globe built with NASA Mars Trek imagery and select a location by clicking or by searching a place name such as Jezero. ATHR then shows:

- Elevation from NASA MGS MOLA topography data

- A local slope estimate computed only from real-measurement pixels

- Nearby Mars 2020 (Perseverance) waypoints and the ordered rover route (Sol, Site, Drive)

- A terrain assessment that reports "insufficient data" or "pending validated thresholds" rather than declaring a site safe

A built-in AI assistant answers questions about the selected location in Arabic or English, with a source list and a confidence level.

HOW IT WORKS

A FastAPI backend reads NASA data through dedicated adapters. When a user asks the assistant a question, the frontend sends the question and the selected point to the backend. The backend retrieves the facts itself and ignores any values sent by the client, so values cannot be faked from the browser. Only these verified facts are passed to a large language model, which explains them in the user's language. The server then returns the answer with sources it built from what was actually retrieved, a confidence level (data-backed, limited or general) and a list of data gaps. The AI key stays on the server and is never exposed in the frontend.

BENEFITS

- One place to explore Mars elevation, slope and rover route data

- Missing data is reported honestly; absence of data is never treated as evidence of safety

- Every answer lists its sources, so users can verify and go deeper

- Arabic and English support, including right-to-left layout

INTENDED IMPACT

To give students, educators and curious explorers an approachable way to understand Mars terrain and missions from real NASA data, and to show a pattern for science AI assistants that stay grounded in retrieved data and admit their limits.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

CesiumJS, JavaScript, HTML and CSS (frontend); Python, FastAPI, Pydantic and HTTPX (backend); an OpenAI-compatible large language model API; Git and GitHub; Render for hosting. No special hardware was used. We used AI assistants to help plan and write parts of the code, as disclosed in the SI section.

CREATIVITY

Instead of letting a chatbot answer from memory, ATHR separates data from language: NASA data is retrieved by our own backend, and the language model only explains it. Sources are attached by the server, not written by the model. The system treats "no data" as a valid, visible result instead of filling gaps, which is rare in AI assistants and especially important for science and mission planning.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

- Scientific honesty: slope is a local estimate (~1.85 km pixels) and is rejected where unreliable, such as near the poles; hazard classification stays undetermined until validated thresholds exist

- Trust: no invented values, no invented sources, no attribution to NASA without evidence

- Security: API key stored as a server environment variable, input validation, clear error messages when the AI service is unavailable

- Accessibility: bilingual interface with RTL support

- Cost and abuse: a free-tier deployment

Source code: https://github.com/malek5p/Athr_NASA
